raw_response:
Let me think this through the way I always do at the start of the season.

I have 10.9 mu total. I keep about 7 mu in the wheat-maize rotation — that's been my main land for years, good soil, close to the well. The other 3.9 mu I plant to cotton. Cotton used to be more profitable here when prices were higher, but I still keep some because the land on that plot is a bit sandier and cotton does alright there.

**Wheat (7 mu, winter):** Last year I put down about two bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15, 50 kg each) per mu before planting, then topdressed with urea at jointing — one bag of urea per mu, maybe a bit more. That comes to around 25 kg of nitrogen per mu all together. Worked fine, got about 450 kg/mu. I'll do the same again. Phosphorus and potassium from the compound fertilizer — about 8 kg each per mu. I irrigate 3 times: once before winter to protect it, once at jointing (that's the important one), once at grain-filling. Spray herbicide in spring, then one pass for aphids and one for rust if the weather is damp. Rotary till after the maize stalks get cleared.

**Maize (7 mu, summer):** Right after wheat harvest I no-till direct seed the maize — saves time because I need to get it in fast before the rains come. Hybrid seed from the township dealer, Zhengdan 958 type, that's what most neighbors plant. About 22-23 kg N per mu (compound at planting plus urea topdress at big flare stage), 6 kg P, 6 kg K. Irrigate twice — at seedling if dry, and at silking. Spray once for armyworm, once for borer. Target 550 kg/mu.

**Cotton (3.9 mu, spring):** Cotton is fussy and expensive on sprays. I use hybrid Bt seed — the bollworm problem is much less than when I was young but you still need resistant varieties. Plough the cotton ground in early spring, that land needs it. About 18 kg N/mu split into base and two topdressings, 7 kg P, 7 kg K. Three irrigations — at squaring, flowering, boll-filling. Pesticide I spray 6 times through the season — aphids early, mirid bugs, spider mites, the usual. Target 240 kg lint per mu.

My thinking: I lean a little on the heavy side with fertilizer, especially nitrogen. A bag of urea is 100 yuan, but a bad harvest on 7 mu of wheat is thousands lost. I'd rather spend the extra 50-100 yuan per mu on fertilizer than gamble. My sons work in town so I do most of this myself with my wife — I need practices that are reliable, not experimental.
